heading: Self-repair also appears under mean and resample ablation
definition: self-repair appears under on-distribution ablations (mean, resample), not only under off-distribution zero ablation.
summary: Several independent groups report supporting evidence, mostly through indirect measures on GPT-2 small's indirect object identification (IOI) task. Independent evidence at 7B covers one counterweight neuron, whose contribution opposes another contribution, and replacing activations with their mean (mean replacement) keeps activations realistic only on average.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B: GPT-2 small, IOI only, independent groups, indirect measures; the originals' baseline is Pythia-160M under resample and mean. Weak R2 at 1-10B: one independent study (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, one counterweight neuron, a swap the verdict equates with class-matched resample) next to the original's resample on Chinchilla 7B. No evidence at 10-100B or >100B, and none in toy models (counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size).
suggested_status.reason: The originals report self-repair under resample ablation (arXiv:2307.15771#R5, Chinchilla 7B) and under resample and mean ablation (arXiv:2402.15390#R12, arXiv:2402.15390#R13, Pythia-160M, LayerNorm ratio). Studies with no author overlap with an original (counts: versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0) report self-repair-related effects under mean, resample, Gaussian or counterfactual replacement. On GPT-2 small IOI: CoAx backup-identification AUC is 0.974±0.002 under mean, 0.961±0.008 under resample and 0.963±0.003 under Gaussian replacement (arXiv:2607.01940#r11, arXiv:2607.01940#r12, arXiv:2607.01940#r13); positive interactions occur under mean and zero ablation (arXiv:2608.19338#r1, arXiv:2608.19338#r2, arXiv:2608.19338#r3, arXiv:2608.19338#r4); NIE is 0.14 versus witness-integrated 1.16 (arXiv:2610.04017#r1). On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, counterweight neuron L27.n13033's erased margin on true statements changes from −2.86 to −0.50 nats at ×1, paired t=15 (arXiv:2610.02173#R5). Counts: versions.V6.verdicts.supports.studies = 4, versions.V6.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 1, versions.V6.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. The limits: the independent measures are indirect and the head-level tests are on IOI. In addition to arXiv:2608.19338's numerical mean/zero comparison, arXiv:2607.01940 Table 7 reports zero, mean, resample and Gaussian arms; these AUC comparisons measure ranking, not restored-output fractions. arXiv:2610.02173's limits_scope verdict says mean ablation is on-distribution only on average.
suggested_status.open_questions: A same-model, same-metric comparison of the restored output fraction under zero vs mean vs resample on general text, by a group other than the originals, would firm up the level. So would results on a model above 10B or in another family (Llama, Gemma, Mistral). The level would move toward C if self-repair under resample shrank to near zero while it stayed large under zero ablation, or if the effect under mean ablation came mainly from the off-manifold pairs that 2610.02173 identifies.

source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

original_result.setup: The authors ablated Pythia-160M head L11H2 on The Pile, selecting the top 2% of 1 million tokens by the head's direct contribution to the output logit.
original_result.result: The clean-to-ablated LayerNorm scale ratio exceeded 1 for 90.66% of selected tokens under resample ablation and 98.75% under mean ablation.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: GPT-2-small backups remained recoverable under mean, resample, and Gaussian replacement.
Neurons opposing predictions shifted toward supporting them under realistic swaps with the opposite class.
GPT-2 small: other components offset disruption when activations were patched from realistic alternative inputs.
GPT-2-small components offset each other's removal under both mean and zero ablation.
Mean ablation pushed activations for many tested IOI and factual pairs beyond the range considered realistic.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Comparing how much self-repair occurs (share of the direct effect restored in the output) under zero vs mean vs resample ablation, in the same model, on general text, with values given in text or tables.
untested.basis: arXiv:2402.15390#R16, arXiv:2402.15390#R17 and arXiv:2402.15390#R18: Figure 5 compares zero, mean and resample ablations without exact restored-output fractions in text. Section 3.2 and its caption explicitly describe positive logit differences under zero ablation, so the qualitative overcorrection finding is not exclusively figure-only. The numerical LayerNorm proxy comparison does not supply the missing restored-output fractions. arXiv:2307.15771#R5 reports restoration under resample only; its untested line states no zero or mean comparison. arXiv:2607.01940#r11, arXiv:2607.01940#r12 and arXiv:2607.01940#r13 report ranking AUC rather than compensation magnitude. arXiv:2608.19338#r1, arXiv:2608.19338#r2, arXiv:2608.19338#r3 and arXiv:2608.19338#r4 compare mean with zero on IOI interaction terms. counts: versions.V6.studies_with_untested_parts = 6.

untested.what: Layer-level (Hydra-style) compensation under zero or mean ablation. The layer-level evidence uses resample ablation only.
untested.basis: 2307.15771 untested line: 'no comparison with zero or mean ablation. Only resample ablation is used.' No other study in the pack ablates whole layers.

untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has only '1-10B', '<1B' and 'not stated' (the not-stated rows are GPT-2 small in 2608.19338 and 2610.04017); there is no 10-100B or >100B bucket.

untested.what: Model families beyond GPT-2, Pythia, Chinchilla and Qwen. Llama, Gemma, Mistral and OLMo have no rows on V6; Gemma is mentioned only in a verdict reason, not in a row.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_family lists GPT-2, 'other or not stated', Pythia, Qwen only.

untested.what: Removal-type ablations (mean or resample) on instruct/chat models. The only instruct model is tested with a patching swap.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_stage has 'not stated' and 'base' only; versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.patching.by_stage has the one instruct/chat entry (2610.02173).

untested.what: Tasks beyond IOI for the independent head-level tests. All three independent GPT-2 studies use IOI; general-text (full-distribution) on-distribution ablations come only from the original 2402.15390 (The Pile).
untested.basis: Row conditions: 2607.01940 r11–r13, 2608.19338 r1–r7 and 2610.04017 r1 all say task=IOI; problems lines of 2608.19338 and 2610.04017 say the setting is narrow.

untested.what: Resample ablation in the head-group interaction setting (mean vs zero only).

wording_issues.issue: 2610.02173's verdict says mean ablation is on-distribution only on average: it puts 40% of IOI pairs (L9.h6) off-manifold. The studies also use other operators that the phrase does not name: template-conditioned mean (2608.19338), moment-matched Gaussian replacement (2607.01940 r13), counterfactual-prompt patching (2610.04017 r1), and a contrastive swap the verdict equates with class-matched resample (2610.02173 R5, R6).

The independent evidence uses measures other than a restored-output fraction: backup-recruitment ranking AUC on GPT-2-small IOI under mean, resample and Gaussian replacement (2607.01940 r11–r13); pairwise interaction terms on GPT-2-small IOI under template-conditioned mean ablation (2608.19338 r1, r3); NIE versus witness-integrated scores on GPT-2-small IOI under counterfactual-prompt patching (2610.04017 r1); and a counterweight neuron's erased margin on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under a matched opposite-class swap at ×1 (2610.02173 R5, R6). For the last measure, opposition shrinks while remaining negative; reversal is not required to observe shrinking opposition. These measures do not report the fraction of output restored.

wording_issues.phrase: not only under off-distribution zero ablation
wording_issues.issue: The available operator comparisons use different measures. On GPT-2-small IOI, 2608.19338 compares template-conditioned mean and zero ablation using pairwise interaction logits (r1–r4); 2607.01940 Table 7 compares zero, mean, resample and Gaussian replacement using backup-ranking AUC (r11–r13 cover the nonzero arms). For Pythia-160M L11H2 on The Pile, filtered to the top 2% of tokens by direct effect, 2402.15390 reports the percentage with LayerNorm scale ratio S/S′ > 1 as 90.66% under resample, 98.75% under mean and 100% under zero ablation (R12–R14). Its Figure 5 gives no exact restored-output fractions in text, but Section 3.2 and the caption explicitly describe zero-ablation overcorrection (R18). That zero arm alone cannot establish repair under other operators.

wording_issues.phrase: Not an artifact of the ablation
wording_issues.issue: The results show the effect is present under other operators, but its size depends on the operator. In 2608.19338, I_PB is 1.080 under mean vs 1.268 under zero, and I_PE is 1.830 under mean vs 1.681 under zero. Zero ablation of Pythia-160M L11H0 can increase the logit difference, i.e. overcorrect (2402.15390 R18). So whether the size of the effect is ablation-specific stays open.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation operator (mean vs zero vs resample vs Gaussian)
method_sensitivity.what: On GPT-2-small IOI, interaction sizes change with the operator, in opposite directions for different group pairs. I_PB is 1.080 logits under template-conditioned mean vs 1.268 under zero (r1, r2). I_PE is 1.830 under mean vs 1.681 under zero (r3, r4). The header says direct interaction magnitudes differ between the two ablations. Backup-recovery AUC changes little across operators: 0.974±0.002 under mean, 0.961±0.008 under resample, 0.963±0.003 under Gaussian (r11–r13). The 2607.01940 header still lists the replacement operator among the settings that change backup recovery.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation method, token filtering and clipping (LayerNorm self-repair)
method_sensitivity.what: Pythia-160M: zero ablation of L11H0 can produce positive logit differences despite positive clean head direct effects (observed overcorrection for V4, R18). That zero-ablation arm alone cannot establish V6 repair under other operators. The resample and mean counterparts are figure-only (R16, R17), and the head label is inconsistent between the prose and the figure (verdict fix). The header says the LayerNorm contribution depends on the ablation method, and that the reported fraction depends on filtering to high-direct-effect tokens and on per-token clipping. A not-in-rows line says GPT2-Small L11H11 shows similar LayerNorm ratios across ablation types (Appendix D).

Responses differ by model, direction and dose. Joint-core interventions can recruit more than single-core ones, and the response saturates beyond full inversion (header). Zero and mean clamps fall at different doses for different pairs (not-in-rows line, Figure 6, Figure 31, App. N), which is the basis of the limits_scope verdict on mean ablation.

Chinchilla 7B: direct and compensatory effects correlate well mainly at intermediate layers (header). The regression slope is below 1 past layer 13 (R3). About 70% of the token-logit reduction is restored at middle layers, where the effects are strongest (R5).

Backup recovery varies with the identity and contamination of the supplied primary set, with output geometry and with task/prompt setting (2607.01940 header). Pinning witnesses has model- and metric-dependent effects: it lowers all three circuit scores on GPT-2 and Llama, but on Qwen3 it improves net and reduces kill and faithfulness (2610.04017 header).

I_PB under template-conditioned mean ablation is 1.080 over four lexical frames (r1) and 1.055 on the original IOI template (r7). The header says the predictive comparison is limited to one template and to mean ablation.
